svg.text: The polar outposts: a research station and a mining camp

Buildings only, no characters; built from World's own shapes in the polar palette: weathered timber and steel, dark roofs, the one warm light steady. Concept art, working labels, pending Legal; city and environment art, so it may be public.
The research station, night: the lit windows
The mining camp, night: the lit windows

Research station: a small cluster raised on posts above the snow: one long main module, two sleeping modules, a generator house with a stack, an instrument mast and a row of fuel drums, joined by a corridor and a snow ramp. Dark

roofs, weathered timber walls, a few steady lit windows. About 14 parts, 360 triangles (estimate), 760 units wide; World's shapes: a slab on posts, two sheds, a block with a chimney, a mast, five octagonal drums.

Mining camp: a headframe over a shaft, an ore bunker with a conveyor to a stockpile of dark rock, a stack of containers, three fuel tanks and a heater shed with a flue. Steel and rusted-brown containers, soot and rock; the heaps

are the darkest, biggest shapes on the white. About 16 parts, 420 triangles (estimate), 900 units wide; World's shapes: a crane, a warehouse, a stepped block, containers, octagonal tanks, a shed with a chimney.

Against the ice (world-light tint applied): the walls (timber and containers) sit 14.6 or more from the white at every key and 17.1 or more from the slate by day; the steel (posts, tanks, small parts) is 11.4 from both, and the

roofs are 19 from the white (they stand against the sky, not the slate). At night everything is dark and the base melts into the slate: a building stands against the sky, not the ground. Nothing is orange (fire's), teal or mid
blue; the warm window light is the city's, steady.
